title: Security advisory: Critical remote code execution vulnerabilities, update now
content:
PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately.

all PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs.Who is at risk:

How to update:

while only an update is a complete solution, the following measures reduce exposure to specific attack paths but do not make an installation safe.If you cannot update immediately:

The advisories linked above have the full technical details.

  • , CVE-2026-109618 (): out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid.RCE via OOM corruptionGHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w
  • , CVE-2026-109619 (): request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it.RCE via stale global stateGHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp
  • Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. Source downloads are on our . Windows source and binaries are .downloads pageon the same page
  • Linux distributions and LTS vendors received the patches in advance, so check your vendor for updated packages.
  • no longer receive updates from the PHP project. Some distributions and LTS vendors provide backported fixes, so contact your vendor for details, or upgrade to a supported version.PHP 8.1 and older
  • If you rely on the volunteer-maintained , we urge you to switch to distribution packages or build from source, so you can immediately apply updates. The repo will not have updates today.rpms.remirepo.net
  • Given the severity of these vulnerabilities, the PHP security team provided minimal source-backports for , , and to help people building from source or without access to an LTS vendor. PHP 7.4PHP 8.0PHP 8.1
  • Set , preferably in a way applications can't override, such as in the FPM pool or Apache configuration, and check that no pool, directory or application setting puts a finite limit back. This removes the controllable PHP memory limit failure, but an underlying allocation failure can still reach the vulnerable path.memory_limit=-1php_admin_value
  • Set a low . For applications that don't require file uploads, set . If file uploads are necessary, set . Keep below . Consider enforcing limits at the web server or proxy level for decoded request size, input field count, multipart part count, header count, and nesting depth. These limits must also cover requests without a usable .post_max_sizepost_max_size = 8Mpost_max_size = 32Mupload_max_filesizepost_max_sizeContent-Length
  • Use a container or cgroup limit as an availability boundary, preferably with a policy that kills only the affected worker. Do not substitute or , as these can cause the vulnerable allocation failure.RLIMIT_ASRLIMIT_DATA
  • Set and restart every worker. Use , an FPM pool or server configuration that applies before request parsing. Do not rely on or FPM . This blocks the confirmed session paths but not other variants.session.upload_progress.enabled=0php.iniini_set().user.ini
  • On PHP 8.5, set and restart every worker. This blocks the confirmed fatal backtrace path only.fatal_error_backtraces=0
  • Remove invalid or deprecated settings applied per request that emit diagnostics before initialization. Hiding diagnostics with , or does not help.error_reportingdisplay_errors@
  • Fix attacker-reachable fatal errors and execution timeouts, including failures in callbacks, upload or import processing and cleanup.
